    Local vertex endomorphism rings of string quotients #

    At a displayed vertex of an admissible monomial bound-quiver quotient, the surviving loops form a basis. Splitting off the trivial loop writes every endomorphism as a scalar identity plus a positive-length tail. Path length is additive under multiplication, while admissibility kills every sufficiently long path, so the positive tail is nilpotent. Consequently the vertex endomorphism ring is local.
